newsitem.title: USA: Seahawk Deep Ocean Tech comes up empty.
newsitem.headline: Seahawk Deep Ocean Tech comes up empty.

text.p: Seahawk Deep Ocean Technology said it came up empty on its latest treasure hunting venture, code named "Golden Eagle," for a 100-year old ship that sunk while transporting gold from the northern to southern areas of the eastern United States.

John Lawrence, chief executive of Seahawk told Reuters "We were extremely disappointed that the ship we dove for and which matched up against our research turned out to be something different. It was the wrong ship. We will continue to search."
Seahawk formed a limited partnership with Eagle Partners Ltd roughly six years ago and then joined with Eagle Miners Inc, a Baltimore based company to conduct the search.
Lawrence said the series of dives lasted over four or five days, at a cost of $3,000 to $4,000 a day. The venture has so far cost the companies $1 million.

Lawrence said through a search of manifests and other archives, "In the worst case scenario, we established that the $400,000 worth of gold coin that sank 100 years ago would today be worth roughly $4 million."
"In the best case scenario," Lawrence added, "depending on the make-up of the coinage, it could be worth $80 million."
